thread.title: AI agents are a 'bane' for some website operators, says Cloudflare

author: TheRegister
title: AI agents are a 'bane' for some website operators, says Cloudflare
text: AI agents are a ‘bane’ for some website operators, says Cloudflare CEO says sovereigns probably exploited PHP2SHELL ages ago, and suggests containers are dead “These vulnerabilities, like the PHP vulnerabilities that were disclosed the other day, had been in the wild for years,” Prince said on the company’s third quarter earnings call. “We're going back through our logs looking for any evidence that hackers or nation-state actors or others had been using them in the past. I know that we're going to find examples of that. ” That was just one of the warnings he offered on the call, among them that some of Cloudflare’s customers believe AI agents are “a bane to their business and want to keep them away.”To explain why, Prince hypothesized that he could use an agent to find him a restaurant to eat at after he finishes his day of investor relations duties.“It might go and scour the internet and look at 1,000 different restaurants' websites, pull down 1,000 different menus, and then I might choose to only go to one of those,” he said. “The problem is that 999 of those restaurants have now had a cost that is just been applied to them, but they are not getting any benefit.” The CEO admitted that web searches have always driven some low-value traffic but feels the volume of agentic activity – which Cloudflare hasPrince also had bad news for Kubernetes aficionados, because he thinks containers might become another casualty of the agentic age. The CEO allowed that containers are “a significant improvement over bare metal or even virtual machines,” and said they fueled the growth of hyperscale clouds and mobile applications. But he thinks containers are already cooked.“The container-based architecture of the hyperscalers and neoclouds just can't keep up in a cost-effective way with the new agentic paradigms of today,” he argued, again citing the 1000:1 ratio of bot:human traffic Cloudflare expects to see online any year now. That’s a Cloudflare-centric view, because Prince pitched the company’s serverless “Workers” service as an alternative to containers.The company also offers products that can either block agents, ameliorate the cost and traffic impacts of agentic activity, or allow organizations to monetize traffic generated by AI. , “approximately five percent” of the web opted in to Cloudflare’s content protection products. The CEO said Meta is already a customer, and said Zuck’s new “Muse” agents will benefit Cloudflare by creating more agentic traffic that third parties want to tame.“It may seem like the sky is falling with the number of new security vulnerabilities that have been reported over the last few weeks,” Prince said. “I wish I could tell you we were through the worst, but we're not. ” He thinks Cloudflare can profit from security misery because the extent of its activities and client base mean it is “among the first to receive quiet disclosure of new vulnerabilities” and remediates them before disclosure.Investors thought this all made sense, and in after-hours trading sent Cloudflare shares up by around 15 percent, meaning it recovered and then improved on losses that it incurred earlier after major US indices dropped around four percent as investors who worry tech stocks are overvalued.®CEO says sovereigns probably exploited PHP2SHELL ages ago, and suggests containers are deadCERT-IN warns of ‘significant escalation’ in AI-powered attacks, some after victims tried to improve defencesPARTNER CONTENT: 300+ AI applications delivering surges in core metrics and annual cost reduction of over CNY100mBritish fintech Revolut slashes AI coding costs 10x by cutting out Claude and going self-hostedAgent orchestration startup gets its exitFirms still want kit on-premises, but spike in revenue is as much about increased costs as higher salesCustomers sweating assets amid tight budgets, as Microsoft execs get creative with sales pitchesRussians are posing as Signal support to launch phishing attacksDEF CON Franklin project enlists hackers to harden critical infrastructure Voting village reports have been so successful, says Jeff Moss, that the whole of DEF CON will now be includedTen years since the first corp ransomware, Mikko Hyppönen sees no end in sightAchieving nirvana: Enlightenment 0.28 hits the desktopUbuntu 27.04 may bring a preview of the long-awaited Core Desktop
